issue_context.title: Incorrect lazy schema for aggregation operation preceded by non-aggregation
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

q = pl.LazyFrame({"a": 1, "b": 1}).group_by("a").agg(pl.col("b").shuffle().first())

print(q.collect_schema())  # [incorrect] Schema({'a': Int64, 'b': List(Int64)})
print(q.collect().collect_schema())  # [expected] Schema({'a': Int64, 'b': Int64})

assert q.collect_schema() == q.collect().collect_schema()

```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

Lazy schema incorrectly implodes the dtype

Regression from 1.12.0 to 1.13.0.


### Expected behavior

See above example

### Installed versions

1.13.0

review_comments: We previously set `agg_list` to `false` (`*nested = nested.saturating_sub(1)`), but then we passed it to `to_field_impl`, so it would get incorrectly overridden by the upper node - this is the cause of the linked issue.
Refactored to use a `bool` indicator - I think we only need to keep track of 2 states
